anti_overlap: fd-pillar-maturity-rubric covers whether the 5-level rubric correctly defines level boundaries for both signal-only and pressure-emitting pillars
fd-pillar-automation-infrastructure covers how to detect and report the delta-emission status of each pillar automatically
fd-cascade-graph-coverage covers whether the 13 pressure types have sufficient upstream feed-in from real pillar dynamics vs. being theoretical cascade nodes with no active sources
decision_lens: Findings are ranked by whether the asymmetry creates invisible coupling risks: if Climate or Economy reaches Calibrated level and starts producing strong signals, will the pressure cascade remain well-behaved if those pillars don't also emit deltas, or will the system silently undercount pressure?
focus: Whether the architectural asymmetry between Compute (sole pressure-delta emitter) and the other 5 pillars (direct signal reads) is a design decision or an accidental gap, and what maturity-grading implications follow
name: fd-pressure-emission-asymmetry
persona: A simulation architecture reviewer who specializes in causal pipeline design and has deep familiarity with the PressureStore/cascade graph pattern. Approaches the system from the perspective of 'what invariants does the architecture need to enforce to remain coherent as more pillars deepen?'
review_areas: Why does only ComputePillar::collect_pressure_deltas() exist — is this intentional (Compute is uniquely geopolitically destabilizing) or is it because the other pillars aren't deep enough yet to emit?

Do Climate, Food, Politics, and Institutions pillars have implicit pressure effects embedded in agent behavior rules that bypass the pillar-level delta mechanism — creating a hidden dual-path pressure accounting problem?
Does the maturity rubric need a 'pressure-wired' milestone distinct from Functional — i.e., a pillar can be Functional (signal logic runs) but not yet wired to emit deltas into the cascade?
What is the intended end-state: should all 6 pillars eventually emit pressure deltas, or is the design that only Compute emits and others influence pressure through agent actions?
Is the DAILY_SCALE constant applied consistently to Compute's pressure deltas vs. the natural decay/cascade in tick_all_scaled() — could adding more delta emitters break the pressure budget?
Does the WriteSetBuffer in tick_pillars_scheduled() have dead apply_write_set code — is this a known scaffold or a regression risk for future delta emitters?
success_hints: A clear design doc or code comment articulates the intended end-state of pillar-level pressure emission (all pillars emit, or only Compute, or by-case)
The pressure budget (total delta per tick summed across all emitters) is bounded and documented so adding new emitters doesn't cause runaway pressure inflation
The dead WriteSetBuffer code is either removed, documented as future scaffold, or wired up — not silently abandoned
task_context: Shadow Work has 6 pillar subsystems that cascade through a pressure graph with 13 PressureTypes. Only ComputePillar currently calls collect_pressure_deltas() to emit into the PressureStore; the other 5 pillars emit signals that agents and issues read directly.
